facts.text: Pettus was originally called Dry Medio until the Civil War, when it was renamed Pettus City in honor of John F. Pettus.
Hodges sold a right‑of‑way to the San Antonio and Aransas Pass Railway and donated the local streets that now form Pettus’s main thoroughfares.
The community sits at the junction of U.S. Route 181 and local roads, a crossroads that has linked it to the rest of Bee County for generations.
Route 181 runs through Pettus, heading south 16 miles to Beeville and north 14 miles to Kenedy, making it a key link between the county seat and the Gulf Coast.
Pettus lies at 28°37′5″N 97°48′8″W, placing it in the northern part of Bee County in south‑central Texas.
